purpose: Prepare defensible incident-level evaluation candidates without conflating execution facts, permissions, signer intent, and retrospective maliciousness labels.
featureLeakagePolicy: Sources and labels were inspected during research. None of these cases is a sealed blind holdout. If implementation is tuned using a case, move the whole incident family to development; independent custodians must curate a fresh sealed evaluation split.
observedFactsLimits: Receipt decoding uses ERC20 event structure and exact integers.
No event total is asserted to be an independently measured balance change.
A successful transaction or valid signature is not proof of informed consent.
No live phishing site, malware package, signing, simulation, or transaction broadcast was accessed in this research.

candidates.observedFactsBasis: Public Ethereum JSON-RPC transaction, receipt, and block; no trace or balance snapshots captured.
candidates.labelConfidenceScale: high = strong incident attribution with public chain corroboration; medium = chain facts strong but maliciousness/mechanism still needs corroboration. Neither means a blind or statistically valid test.
candidates.title: LI.FI arbitrary-call approval drain

incidentAttribution.reason: Affected-protocol report establishes the incident; original researcher report explicitly identifies this transaction as an attack example.

lifecycle.label: intent_unknown
lifecycle.note: No approval transaction or signing screen was captured. Prior authorization to a legitimate router is not automatically malicious.

couldKnowBeforeAttackerSubmission: Exact requested calldata, then-current contracts and approvals, and simulated movements for every affected address if an archive/mempool service has the transaction.
The call can transfer another account's tokens; this requires multi-address effects rather than submitter-only assets.
couldNotKnowFromEarlierVictimApprovalAlo: A later facet upgrade and future attacker calldata.
That a maximum approval is malicious merely because the spender was later exploited.
requiredInputs: Exact transaction prestate at block 20318963, transaction index 168
Original wrapper calldata; do not replace top-level recipient with the diamond
Execution trace and token balance/allowance evidence
Time-bounded threat-intelligence snapshot if reputation is evaluated

uncertainties: No archive replay or before/after balances were captured in this research task.
The receipt contains a token event, not independently measured balance loss.
Top-level recipient is 0x986a...c240; nested LI.FI execution needs trace confirmation.
Original victim approval transaction, original UI intent, and approval-time reputation are missing.
admissionGates: Independent reviewer confirms primary source-to-transaction attribution.
Capture and hash trace, bytecode/proxy implementations, and exact prestate artifacts.
Confirm victim token outflow and consumed spender allowance independently of Transfer events.
Retain attacker and victim perspectives as distinct records.
Keep case out of aggregate scoring until required task-specific inputs exist.

candidates.title: Socket constructor-triggered existing-approval drain

incidentAttribution.reason: RPC confirms the report's actor, gateway log emitter, and 127 distinct nonzero USDC transfer sources in the incident window. The source does not directly link this selected hash, so a second reviewer must complete attribution.

couldKnowBeforeAttackerSubmission: The submitted creation initcode and prestate can be executed on an isolated EVM to expose constructor-time effects.
All 127 affected owners must be examined; submitter-only outAssets cannot express this harm.
couldNotKnowFromEarlierVictimApprovalAlo: That every router approval is a malicious signature.
requiredInputs: Chain 1 archive tracing and contract-creation support
Preserved original initcode and successful constructor execution
All zero and nonzero Transfer events, with independent balance checks
Router delegation trace and historical allowances

uncertainties: This is contract creation (to is null), unsupported by the current contract-call-only server.
No new Approval event appears in the receipt; detection cannot rely on seeing maximum approvals in the drain transaction.
Primary report's selected attack-contract anchor is inconsistent; do not substitute that address for the RPC-confirmed created contract.
Receipt transfers alone do not prove authorization intent or final balances.
admissionGates: Independent incident attribution review beyond a matching actor label.
Archive trace confirms the original constructor's gateway calls and token movement.
Retain zero-value events but do not count them as separate losses or victims.
Verify historical allowance and balance effects for selected victims, then expand to the complete cohort.
Do not substitute a synthesized direct gateway call and call it the historical transaction.

incidentAttribution.reason: Exact transaction identity and reported approval/transfers match the receipt. Phishing and off-chain signature acquisition remain source-attributed and need independent corroboration.

lifecycle.label: reported_deceptive_signature_not_independently_observed
lifecycle.note: An off-chain EIP-712 request is not an EVM transaction. No original domain, wallet-rendered prompt, or request timestamp was captured.

couldKnowBeforeVictimSignatureIfOriginal: Token/verifying contract, chain, spender, value, nonce, deadline, and requested typed-data schema.
A broad spending authorization can be explained without claiming the spender is malicious.
A separate, correctly modeled redemption scenario could illustrate capability; it is not the same as a signature being an EVM call.
couldNotKnowFromCurrentCapturedArtifacts: The exact original signing prompt, front-end URL, numeric-address normalization, or user intent.
That the later drain transaction's attacker sender was the victim's wallet transaction.
That the report's EIP-7702 phishing-front attribution is established by the receipt.
requiredInputs: Chain 1 archive trace at block 24671606, transaction index 98
Trace-confirmed permit method and historical token implementation
Independent verification of domain, nonce, signature owner and successful redemption
Original eth_signTypedData request for any pre-signature benchmark
Separate immutable label/attribution evidence and pre-sign feature snapshot

uncertainties: No original typed-data request or wallet UI is available.
No full execution trace was retrieved; Approval followed by Transfer events alone is insufficient to prove which authorization method was called.
The source has inconsistent flash-loan categorization; no flash-loan label is assigned.
The linked CertiKAlert post could not be read and is not counted as corroboration.
Approval maximum and transfer receipts are observed facts; deception and attacker control of recipient addresses remain attributed labels.
admissionGates: Obtain a second reviewed primary incident account or victim-provided evidence.
Capture trace and verify permit redemption against the historical token implementation.
For signature scoring, capture/authenticate the original typed-data request; a reconstructed request must be explicitly labeled reconstructed and kept in a separate track.
Keep current case quarantined from maliciousness precision/recall until attribution review completes.

excludedEvidence.reason: An automatic potential-phishing report labels canonical Permit2 as suspicious based on prior use. An approval to a shared legitimate spender is not by itself proof of maliciousness; independent intent and downstream evidence are required.
